answer: Each identity registers one voyage in a sonnet register: 14 fields naming vessel, route, departure tide, port stamp, and identity key, plus an 80-credit bond. A tide auditor recomputes the register against the tide table and stamp log; a missing field, reused stamp, or tide time outside the window burns the bond. The first fee is 28 credits, the kth costs 28+6(k-1), so the 1,000th costs 6,022; 1,000 fakes pay 3,025,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-voyage ring fails because one stamp cannot validate two sonnet registers. An honest agent registers once and recovers the bond after audit.
